lineage: Provenance: the construction follows the published glv-six-class-rho-secp-v1b (submission 189ebc42, in review, declared as a dependency), itself a port of the published BLS12-381 glv-six-class-rho-v11 (submission 1c600df4, also declared). Every algebraic identity, instruction itemisation, bound and toy result below is restated and re-verified in THIS package's own proof.md and experiment.py; nothing is inherited by citation. v2n tightens three accounting constants only: the ordinary-step charge 1.20 -> 1.18 (the published itemisation is 159 instructions; v1 charged a 200-instruction budget, v2 charges 180); the walk-slowdown allowance kappa 1.05 -> 1.04 (every published and new toy measurement is inside +1.3% of the model mean); the H1 budget quantile floor 0.395 -> 0.396 (K = ln(1/0.604)).
work_function: W_max = 2^127.038 target-group-operation equivalents enforced by a global work meter on every run; phase 1 = 1.18*(S_ops + 2^60) with S_ops = 1.04*sqrt(2N'*ln(1/0.604)), N' = N*2048/2047, N = (r-1)/6; hard extras < 2^97.56; expected random extras < 2^113.9 against headroom > 2^121.3, so the Markov early-halt probability is < 0.0058 and success >= 0.396 - 0.0058 = 0.3902 > 0.39. Score = 127.038.
heuristics: H1 as in the published package: random mapping on N = (r-1)/6 classes with the Brent-Pollard correction and a 4% slowdown allowance; partition, distinguished and routing bits pseudo-random functions of the class; non-fruitless returns at most L_max^2/(2N) per trail; canonical twist index uniform and independent of the partition index. Supported by our toy runs at the v2 budget: every configuration clears the 0.396 floor by at least 0.017, and the long-trail trap test separates the doubling escape from the additive control (0/150 vs 105/150 at R = 4).
limitations: H1 is a heuristic supported at toy scale only.
This is a generic attack, not a practical break.
